 Embassy in Madrid yet to confirm if Malaysians involved in high-speed rail crash
 Wednesday, 28 Oct 2026
 | 9:05 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Embassy in Madrid is in contact with Spanish authorities to determine whether any Malaysians were involved in a train crash in Spain in which at least 30 have been killed.
 Wisma Putra said the embassy has not confirmed whether any Malaysians were involved in the deadly collision between two high-speed trains.
 The incident on Wednesday (Oct 28) is the second deadly accident in less than a year.
 ALSO READ:  At least 30 people killed in Spain when two high-speed trains collide 
 In January, two high-speed trains belonging to the same operators, on the same line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region, killed 46 people.
 Footage from regional ⁠Castilla-La Mancha television showed a derailed train with several carriages remaining on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath ‌the line.
